6792.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
6792.question_text: If stationery bought for N200 has been entered as N2000. To correct this error?
6792.explanation:
To correct the error, we have to debit the amount in excess so as when it is being calculated, the debit side would balance with the credit side. 

Remember income in recorded on the debit side while expenses are recorded on the credit side. Since stationary was bought, (expense) it is assumed that it was recorded on the credit side. hence we will debit the amount in excess

6793.question_text: The account which refers to the tangible assets of a company that is of permanent nature is the?
6793.explanation: Real account is an account dealing with the material assets of a business, such as its property.

6795.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
6795.explanation:
A credit note is one of the source documents used by a business. It is a receipt given by a seller to a buyer. 

Credit notes are typically used when there has been an error in an already-issued invoice, such as an incorrect amount, or when a customer wishes to change their original order

6796.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
6796.question_text: A major cause of discrepancy between bank statement and the cash book that overstates the bank statement balance is the?
6796.explanation: Electronic charges or payment on the bank statement not yet recorded in the cashbooks can cause discrepancies on the cash book. If interest has being paid on the account and not recorded of the cashbook, the bank statement is likely going to be overstated with the amount paid and not recorded

6797.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
6797.question_text: The bank charges levied on a current account holder is the charge on?
6797.explanation: Charge on turnover (COT) also known as Commission on turnover are charges a customer incurs for debit transactions (transaction involving withdrawals and/or operating cost to the bank) from his current account.

6798.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
6798.question_text: The course of discrepancies between the bank statement and the cash book that overstates the cash book is the?
6798.explanation: Uncredited cheques: These are cheques received from customers and other sources for which the firm has banked but the bank has not yet availed the funds by crediting the firm's account. In this case, the cash book balance will be more than the bank balance

6802.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
6802.question_text:
Use the information below to answer questions 

Sundry debtor..................N20,000
Provision for bad debts........N500

Provision for bad debt at 4% of sundry debtors.

Determine the provision for bad debts to profit and loss account?
6802.explanation:
The business owner made a provision of 500 as bad debt. Total debt owed was 20,000. At the end of the period, bad debts was 4%. Hence we have; 

4% x 20000
0.04 x 20000 = 800

we subtract the total bad debt from the amount that was initially provided for bad debt and charge it to the profit and loss account as a expense

Provision for bad debts = 500
800 - 500 = 300

6821.question_text: The salary of a partner is usually debited to the?

44394.question_text: If Fatima was granted a discount of 2% what will be discount allowed?

44395.subject: Accounts - Principles of Accounts
44395.question_text: Calculate the cash balance after the discount
44395.explanation:
cash balance = debit side of the cash column - credit side of cash column. Hence we have;

Discount allowed = 0.02 x 2000 = 40

Debit column = 3000 + 1000 + 2000 + 200 = 6200 
6200 - 40 (cash discount) = 6160

credit column = 200 + 3000 + 200 = 3400

6160 - 3400 = 2760
